locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this store guarantees that a successful save is visible to later loads? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The write quorum is Math.floor(N/2), which for N=3 is 1 and for N=5 is 2. Read quorum is floor(N/2)+1, so W + R = N, not more than N. A save can succeed after reaching only a minority, and a later load can hit a majority that contains no replica holding that write, returning an older ticket version (for example a reassigned ticket appearing unassigned). The write quorum must also be a majority (floor(N/2)+1) so W + R > N and every read set overlaps every write set.

choiceQuestions.prompt: With 5 replicas, two of which are down, what happens when load() is called?
choices: It throws QuorumError because any unavailable replica fails the read
It succeeds if the 3 reachable replicas respond within the timeout, returning the highest-version record among them
It returns null because the down replicas are counted as missing records
It waits until the down replicas recover before returning
choiceQuestions.explanation: Rejected or timed-out replicas are dropped by the status === "fulfilled" filter; only responses.length < readQuorum (3) throws. With 3 healthy responders the read proceeds and picks the highest version. It does not fail on any single outage, does not treat failures as null records (only fulfilled 404s become null), and withTimeout ensures it never waits indefinitely.

choiceQuestions.prompt: How does a replica's response of HTTP 500 to put() affect the ack count in save()?
choices: It counts as an ack because the promise fulfilled
It causes save() to throw immediately
It is not counted, because put() resolves to false and only fulfilled results with value true are counted
It is retried once before being counted
choiceQuestions.explanation: HttpReplicaClient.put returns res.ok, so a 500 resolves to false. save() counts only results where status is fulfilled and value === true. Fulfillment alone is not enough, nothing throws until the total is compared with the quorum, and there is no retry logic.

choiceQuestions.prompt: What is a consequence of load() calling repair() with void instead of awaiting it?
choices: Read latency is not increased by repair writes, but a repair failure is silently ignored and stale replicas may stay stale until a later read
Repair writes may overwrite newer data because putIfNewer is not version-aware
The returned record may be older than what repair writes
Unhandled promise rejections will crash the process whenever a replica is down
choiceQuestions.explanation: repair runs in the background, so callers do not wait on it; it uses Promise.allSettled so failures do not reject and are simply dropped. putIfNewer sends an if-version-below header so newer data is not overwritten, the returned record is exactly what repair writes, and allSettled prevents unhandled rejections.
